Bitcoin is ending November down about 23% — its worst month since 2022.

It finished October above $77,000. On Friday it closed just under $60,000, a level it hadn't seen since October 2024. Per Opening Bell Daily, that 22.7% drop is roughly six times the S&P 500's 3.7% decline this month.

Here's the money part. A 2025 executive order and a 2026 Labor Department rule opened U.S. 401(k) plans to crypto. So for the first time, a swing like this can land in a retirement account, not just a trading app.

My take: a 23% month is normal for bitcoin and that's the whole point. Fine for money you can lose, hard to stomach on the account you retire on.

Would you ever hold crypto in your 401(k)? 👇

Source: Opening Bell Daily (Nov. 28, 2026)
